Dear Tom,
 
Thank you for your reply. I spoke with the office lawyers yesterday as instructed by the management, and they confirmed the payment amount of around $1540. However, another invoice was suddenly added afterward. I also reached out to the property management, but the manager has not responded to my acknowledged my concerns. The new invoice appears vague, and I only received communication about it today. 
 
Despite my first letter being issued on July 29. I have been trying to cooperate and make payment, but the amount now differs from what was confirmed. It feels like the process is being handled unfairly, and I would like to know where I can raise my concerns formally. Please help clarify this matter so I can proceed with payment today as agreed. Sincerely,

Subject: Re: Re: PSCC 754: Second Notice- Infractions of Corporation's Rules- Pet Removal & Room Accomodations
 
Dear Management,
 
I am writing to formally request clear, written clarification regarding my rights and responsibilities as the legal owner of my two-bedroom condominium unit.
 
As previously reported to your office by phone, in writing, and again today in person with the receptionist, I have removed all unauthorized individuals and their two dogs from the unit. The unit currently has only three occupants, which is under the legal and standard occupancy limit for a two-bedroom apartment that allows up to four people.
 
As the sole owner of this condominium, I have the right to decide who may reside with me, provided I follow any official procedures required by the building. Whether an individual chooses to stay or leave is a private matter between myself and those I agree to live with. This is not a management-run occupancy system; it is an owner-occupied residence.
 
At this time, one current resident has given me notice, but I am unsure whether he will leave by the date he indicated, as he has mentioned personal circumstances involving his young son and the possibility of needing additional time. For this reason, I need clarity on whether he must be registered, and if so, what the proper process is.
 
In addition, I need confirmation for future situations. I purchased this property so that I would have the ability, when necessary, to rent out a room for financial support. I am currently not working and am recovering from a brain stroke, and the option to rent a room occasionally is important for my stability and well-being. Therefore, I must understand exactly what is allowed and what procedures I must follow, so that I can plan responsibly and comply with the building’s requirements.
 
Accordingly, I request detailed clarification on the following:
 
1. What are my rights as the legal owner in choosing who may reside in my unit?
 
 
2. At what point does the building require an occupant to be registered, and what is the official definition of a long-term occupant in this condominium?
 
 
3. What is the exact procedure for registration, including any documentation or identification required?
 
 
4. Are owners permitted to have roommates or room rentals, provided the unit remains within occupancy limits and building rules?
 
 
5. Are there any bylaws or rules restricting owners from renting a room in a one-bedroom, two-bedroom, or studio unit? If so, please provide them in writing.
 
 
 
I also request assistance with activating my FOB, as proper access to the building is necessary for my security and daily functioning.
 
I respectfully request a timely written response so that I may ensure full compliance with building requirements while maintaining my rights as the property owner.
 
Thank you for your attention and cooperation.
 
Amit
647-717-0929

Subject: PSCC 754: Infractions of Corporation's Rules- Pet Removal
 
Good Afternoon,
We hope this email finds you well.
Please find attached a formal letter regarding non-compliance with the Corporation’s Rules related to a pet residing in Unit 432.
As per the Corporation’s Declaration and Rules, pets are strictly limited to the following:
“No animals, reptiles, rodents, livestock or fowl of any kind shall be permitted within any unit or common area, other than one (1) pet per dwelling unit, with the term ‘pet’ being defined restrictively to include only:
i) A canary, a budgie, or any other small bird that is kept in a cage at all times;
ii) A hamster, a gerbil, a guinea pig, or a rabbit that is kept in a cage at all times;

Legal Infractions and Breaches

Section 17(3) – The corporation has a duty to take reasonable steps to ensure compliance with the Act, declaration, by-laws, and rules. Selective or punitive enforcement fails this obligation.
Section 37(1) – Directors and officers (including agents such as property managers) must act honestly, in good faith, and exercise reasonable care and diligence. The actions described reflect a failure to meet this standard.
 
Section 119 – Owners are required to comply with rules; however, enforcement must be reasonable, consistent, and not arbitrary. The current actions appear selective and disproportionate.
 
Section 134 – Compliance and enforcement actions (including legal steps) must be reasonable and justified. Escalating to legal notices under these circumstances may constitute abuse of this provision.
 
Section 135 – Oppression remedy: conduct that is oppressive, unfairly prejudicial, or unfairly disregards the interests of an owner. The pattern of financial pressure, delays, and selective enforcement may meet this threshold.
